run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/checkout since 2026-11-15T01:49:06Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/checkout is driven by checkout's own failed oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder spans: 866.03 ERROR-status PlaceOrder spans against 2022.08 non-error ones in the 00:49:06–02:29:21Z window (~30%), 12–42% per 5-minute interval. Each failure carries gRPC status 13 INTERNAL with the message 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 400'; the frontend converts it to HTTP 500 for the load-generator. The failing traces show the checkout 'HTTP POST' client span to the shipping service's /get-quote failing; shipping answered in tens of microseconds, never called the quote service (no 'POST quote' span), and returned far before it logged the next 'Requesting quote' line. Failing checkouts also contain no ProductCatalogService/GetProduct or CurrencyService/Convert spans (aggregate counts scale with successful PlaceOrders, not with all PlaceOrders), so the requests being checked out had empty item lists, and the shipping quote call was the first and only failing step. The email service is not shown to be failing: its POST /send_order_confirmation count tracks successful PlaceOrders, no email span carries an error status, and sampled email spans are http.status_code 200 — so the 'email service' wording in the error text is not corroborated. Partial because the exact 400 branch inside shipping, and the origin of the email wording, remain unresolved, and no pre-alert baseline exists (metric samples start at 01:49:06Z, the alert's start time).

claims.text: In 2026-11-15T00:49:06Z–02:29:21Z checkout produced 866.03 ERROR-status spans on oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and 866.03 on its client span 'HTTP POST', against 2022.08 PlaceOrder spans without error status (about 30% of PlaceOrder spans errored).

The PlaceOrder error share per 5-minute window varied: 70 errors vs 284.4 non-error (01:54:06Z), 146.7 vs 201.1 (~42%, 01:59:06Z), 32.2 vs 226.7 (~12%, 02:09:06Z), and 40.9 vs 125.1 in the last window ending 02:29:06Z.

The first returned sample of the checkout error-rate range query is 01:49:06Z (the alert's start time) and the first non-zero 5-minute error count is at 01:54:06Z, so this data source holds no error-rate reading before the alert started.

Failing checkout spans carry otel.status_description and an exception.message of exactly 'shipping quote failure: failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 400' with rpc.grpc.status_code 13 (INTERNAL); the frontend records the same '13 INTERNAL: ...' message and returns HTTP 500 to the load-generator's POST.

In the failing traces the checkout 'HTTP POST' client span is an error whose visible child is shipping's /get-quote server span, completed in 31–469 µs with no status tag and no child spans (trace 6bda…: client span 1,726 µs error, shipping /get-quote 37 µs starting 1.2 ms into the client span).

shipping recorded 2884.6 /get-quote spans but only 2019.4 'POST quote' client spans in the window (~865 /get-quote calls never called quote), while the quote service recorded 2019.9 POST /getquote spans with no ERROR status.

Failing checkout traces contain no oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and no oteldemo.CurrencyService/Convert spans, while successful traces do; per-5m checkout GetProduct counts (540, 323.3, 281.1 …) track non-error PlaceOrder counts (284.4, 225.6, 201.1 …) rather than all PlaceOrder spans, and CartService/GetCart is one per PlaceOrder — so the failing PlaceOrders had empty item lists.

shipping's retained log lines are only 'Requesting quote', 'Sending Quote' and 'Tracking ID Created': the read of 01:53:18–01:53:22Z shows requests at 01:53:18.585Z, 01:53:18.685Z and then 01:53:22.188Z, with no line at 01:53:20.016Z when the failed /get-quote of trace 6bda… was served; the read of 01:53:19–01:53:40Z shows only the same routine lines (36 lines) and nothing for the failed quote call.

The email service recorded 2013.8 POST /send_order_confirmation spans with no ERROR status; sampled email spans carry http.status_code 200; its per-5m request counts track non-error PlaceOrder counts (289 vs 284.4, 220 vs 225.6, 200 vs 201.1, 217 vs 216.7), so no extra or failed email calls are visible.

No ERROR-status spans were returned for shipping, email, quote, cart, currency or product-catalog; the window's error breakdown is checkout 1732.06, frontend 3245.71, frontend-proxy 53374.54, ad 3.06, fraud-detection 3.05, recommendation 4.06, accounting 0, payment 0.

frontend error spans match the checkout failures one-for-one: POST /api/checkout 864.17, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout 864.17, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 864.17, POST 653.2, and 0 for GET, GET/POST /api/cart, GET /api/data, AdService/GetAds, CartService/AddItem, CartService/GetCart and tcp.connect.
frontend-proxy error spans are dominated by operation 'ingress' (52805.3) with only 569.25 on 'router frontend egress', so the bulk of its error spans is not the frontend request path.

checkout, email, shipping and quote pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0, created 2026-11-15T01:38:57Z–01:38:59Z with single containers; the only events in the window are the load-generator ReplicaSet rollout at 02:13:12–02:13:13Z (SuccessfulCreate and SuccessfulDelete for load-generator-7d5756fbd9-zzj4z / load-generator-c7cbc4c99-xlnk2, ScalingReplicaSet 0→1 and 1→0).

A cart log line 'GetCartAsync called with userId=' (empty user id) at 01:53:20.1608023Z coincides with the failing trace 6bda…'s checkout GetCart span start at 01:53:20.160834Z; the other inspected failing trace c7625… (PlaceOrder 01:53:40.465Z, GetCart 01:53:40.485Z) matched 'GetCartAsync called with userId=9f5f8f6a-…' at 01:53:40.4851719Z.

The alert is caused by PlaceOrder attempts with empty carts: checkout calls CartService/GetCart, receives no items (hence no product-catalog or currency lookups), still POSTs the shipping quote, that POST fails, and checkout returns gRPC 13 INTERNAL, which the frontend turns into HTTP 500; these attempts account for the ~30% PlaceOrder error share.

The 400 is produced inside the shipping service before any downstream call — a local rejection of the quote request (candidate condition: empty item list) — because the /get-quote span ends within tens of microseconds with no child span, the quote service never sees those requests, and shipping logs no entry for them.

The failing span's text attributes the 400 to a POST to the email service, but the email service shows no failed or extra requests: its POST /send_order_confirmation count equals successful PlaceOrders, no email span carries an error status, and no retained email span carries http.status_code 400, so the email attribution is uncorroborated.

frontend-proxy's large error volume is not tied to the checkout failures: 52805.3 of its error spans are 'ingress' spans while only 569.25 are 'router frontend egress' spans, whereas each sampled failed checkout shows exactly one ingress and one router-egress 500 span.

An email-service failure as the cause of the checkout error rate is rejected: email served about one request per successful order with no error-status spans or 4xx evidence, and the failing call's visible callee is shipping's /get-quote.

shipping or quote pod crashes/restarts/resource pressure are rejected as the cause: both pods are Running and ready with restartCount 0, no Evicted/OOMKilled/Unhealthy events were returned, and their successful path keeps serving (2019.4 quote calls, no ERROR-status spans).

The load-generator rollout at 02:13:12Z did not cause the error rate: it was a controller-driven replacement (new pod …-zzj4z with restartCount 0, SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete and ScalingReplicaSet events), and checkout PlaceOrder error spans are present in every 5-minute interval from 01:54:06Z through 02:29:06Z, before and after that rollout.

Have the owners of shipping and checkout confirm the /get-quote handling of empty item lists (why a 400 is returned instead of a zero-value quote) and where the 'failed POST to email service: expected 200, got 400' wording is generated, since telemetry alone cannot resolve that branch.

Check whether the frontend/load-generator sometimes issues checkout without a user/session id (an empty userId cart lookup was observed at one failure) and decide whether an empty-cart checkout should be reported as a client error rather than inflating the server error-rate alert.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate rule could not be retrieved from Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules with rule_name RequestErrorRate returned no data, evidence_id f4cf886b-2e8a-4938-8ae8-ebafc6edbc48-t0:355819f8-ee76-49db-afb7-f02b4e2f14ad), so its exact expression/threshold is unknown; the '0.2' figure exists only in the alert annotation.

No error-rate reading exists before 01:49:06Z (first returned sample equals the alert start) and the retained Jaeger data covers only about 01:51:43Z–01:53:56Z, so the true onset and a pre-incident baseline cannot be established.

Email log reads returned no data for both the unfiltered and filtered query (c32ce745-c5c8-4539-a061-96d0a39f67a3-t0:acc2f721-d8ce-4adf-95a3-721f64c3ddc7, e7348054-50f4-44e1-9cbd-1159417e1938-t1:f25a5a37-3976-4b80-bb05-fb85e2195deb), so email application logs could not be checked and a 4xx in email cannot be excluded from logs; the search for email spans tagged http.status_code=400 also returned no data (f4cf886b-2e8a-4938-8ae8-ebafc6edbc48-t1:a969c027-53ed-441f-b552-f4f7f141b60e).

The shipping error-filtered log query returned no data (c32ce745-c5c8-4539-a061-96d0a39f67a3-t1:b5db7e02-0ec7-4aff-a720-6246d1b7307d), and the checkout error-filtered log query returned no data (f0aa8ff0-2416-46bf-8338-c66580f69f32-t1:290ed108-74f7-4134-a8d4-0bf7551bd8a6); a filter miss is not proof those services logged no errors.

No shipping log line and no error-status span exists for the failed /get-quote calls, and application source code is not available, so the exact code path that returns the 400 and the origin of the 'email service' wording remain unknown.

Two of the five sampled failing traces lack the checkout 'HTTP POST' and shipping /get-quote spans entirely (one has an invisible parent span), leaving span-export gaps that make per-request call chains unknown in those cases.
Why the checked-out carts were empty is only partly supported (one timestamp coincidence with an empty userId cart lookup); load-generator session behaviour was not verified.

The change_history integration is not integrated in this Run, so no deployment/configuration change record can be checked; current pod state (all service pods created 01:38:57–01:38:59Z, restartCount 0) is a query-time observation, not proof of the state during earlier parts of the window.
flagd's configmap shows all documented flags at defaultVariant off at query time and contains no email- or shipping-failure flag, but its content at incident time could not be verified.

The load-generator error-series query returned no data (f57925cf-2e6e-4488-9c45-4973357f5ab1-t1:4881b30e-417d-4c21-8aab-9b2933f128f7) and the namespace events view carried only Normal events at 02:13:12–02:13:13Z (eaecb4c6-c459-4609-9fc9-9da9a4ab5242-t1:8cbcbe88-6d59-41c5-9aa0-2e3fb0b2626d returned no non-Normal events), so warnings/evictions older than retention are unknown.
next_steps: Review shipping's /get-quote implementation and checkout's HTTP client error construction to confirm which condition returns 400 and why the message names the email service.
Confirm whether checkouts without a user/session id are expected from the frontend and load generator, and whether empty carts should be rejected earlier as client errors.
Enable or collect email-service application logs (currently no data) to conclusively confirm it never returns 400 during this window.
Review the RequestErrorRate alert rule and its error-rate definition so the observed ~30% PlaceOrder failure share can be reconciled with the annotation value 0.2.
